topic: Top 50 Most Used Firearms and Weapon Systems in the Russia-Ukraine War (2022-present)
methodology: Three parallel research agents searched different weapon categories: (1) infantry firearms/small arms, (2) anti-tank weapons/RPGs/grenade launchers/MANPADS, (3) artillery/mortars/heavy crew-served weapons. Results merged and deduplicated. Confidence recalculated based on cross-agent agreement: 3 agents = high, 2 agents = medium, 1 agent = low. Ranked by prevalence (widespread > common > limited) then confidence.

top_50.name: AK-74M
top_50.notes: Standard service rifle of Russian Ground Forces; also widely in Ukrainian inventory from Soviet-era stocks.

top_50.name: PKM
top_50.notes: Standard GPMG of both armies. Used for infantry support, vehicle mounting, and on robotic platforms.

top_50.name: Dragunov SVD
top_50.notes: Standard squad-level marksman rifle. One per infantry squad in Soviet/Russian doctrine.

top_50.name: Makarov PM
top_50.notes: Legacy Soviet sidearm still ubiquitous on both sides. Millions in stock.

top_50.name: RPG-7 / RPG-7V2
top_50.notes: Described as 'ubiquitous' on the battlefield. Reusable launcher with HEAT, thermobaric, and fragmentation warheads.

top_50.name: GP-25 / GP-30
top_50.notes: Standard under-barrel grenade launchers for AK-74 family rifles. Used extensively by both sides.

top_50.name: AGS-17 Plamya
top_50.notes: Standard automatic grenade launcher of both armies. Tripod or vehicle-mounted. 350-400 rpm.

top_50.name: DShK / DShKM
top_50.notes: WWII-era HMG still widely used on vehicle mounts and for anti-drone fire.

top_50.name: NSV Utyos
top_50.notes: Soviet HMG replacing DShK. Used vehicle-mounted (NSVT) and on infantry tripods.

top_50.name: BM-21 Grad
top_50.notes: Most numerically prevalent MLRS. Russia had ~3,000 total; Ukraine ~185. Used for area suppression.

top_50.name: 2S19 Msta-S
top_50.notes: Russia's primary SPH and backbone of Russian artillery. 293+ confirmed losses.

top_50.name: 2S1 Gvozdika
top_50.notes: Light tracked SPH used extensively due to massive Soviet stockpiles.

top_50.name: 2S3 Akatsiya
top_50.notes: Russia had ~1,500 total; Ukraine ~249. Huge portion of both armies' SPH fleet.

top_50.name: D-30 Howitzer
top_50.notes: Light, versatile howitzer. Russia had ~4,550 total. Cheap, reliable, and plentiful.

top_50.name: 2A65 Msta-B
top_50.notes: Russia had ~750 total; Ukraine ~130. Both sides rely on this as primary towed 152mm gun.

top_50.name: 2B11 / 2S12 Sani
top_50.notes: Standard heavy mortar of both armies at battalion level.

top_50.name: 2B14 Podnos
top_50.notes: Standard company/battalion mortar. Man-portable for light infantry. Range ~4 km.

top_50.name: FGM-148 Javelin
top_50.notes: Most prominent Western ATGM. 8,500+ delivered. Fire-and-forget, top-attack mode.

top_50.name: NLAW
top_50.notes: 4,000+ delivered from UK. Critical in early 2022 defense of Kyiv.

top_50.name: Stugna-P
top_50.notes: Ukrainian-produced ATGM. Remote-control firing for operator survivability. Range 4 km.

top_50.name: 9M133 Kornet
top_50.notes: Russia's primary heavy ATGM. 1,200mm+ RHA penetration. Immune to electronic countermeasures.

top_50.name: RPG-22 Netto
top_50.notes: One of the most common RPGs in Russian army inventory. Used by both sides.

top_50.name: RPG-26 Aglen
top_50.notes: Along with RPG-22, the most common disposable RPG in Russian service. 500mm RHA penetration.

top_50.name: FIM-92 Stinger
top_50.notes: 2,000+ delivered. Key tool against Russian helicopters in early phases.

top_50.name: 9K38 Igla
top_50.notes: Soviet-era shoulder-fired SAM used by both sides. Downed a Russian Su-25 in June 2024.

top_50.name: Piorun (Grom-2M)
top_50.notes: Polish-made. Attributed with most MANPADS kills in the conflict. 3,500+ supplied.

top_50.name: AK-12
top_50.notes: Next-gen Russian service rifle. First large-scale combat in Ukraine 2022.

top_50.name: AKM / AK-47
top_50.notes: Pulled from deep stockpiles for mobilized reserves, Wagner, and territorial defense.

top_50.name: AKS-74U
top_50.notes: Used by vehicle crews, officers, and special units. Being replaced by Western SMGs.

top_50.name: Kord (6P50)
top_50.notes: Modern Russian HMG replacing NSV. Mounted on modern Russian tanks.

top_50.name: M2 Browning
top_50.notes: US-supplied HMG on vehicles and static positions. Demand doubled globally.

top_50.name: HK416
top_50.notes: 4,750+ delivered. Used by Ukrainian SSO/HUR special operations forces.

top_50.name: CZ Bren 2 (Sich)
top_50.notes: Primary weapon of Ukrainian Marine Corps. Czech-supplied.

top_50.name: FN SCAR-L/H
top_50.notes: ~4,000 delivered. SCAR-H used in marksman roles.

top_50.name: M777 Howitzer
top_50.notes: ~152-198 delivered. Most numerous Western towed howitzer. Over 1/3 damaged by mid-2023.

top_50.name: 2S22 Bohdana
top_50.notes: Ukrainian-produced wheeled SPH. 150+ built by 2024; ~40% of Ukraine's frontline artillery.

top_50.name: M109 (variants)
top_50.notes: ~90 systems from Norway, Belgium, Italy, Latvia, and US. Workhorse Western SPH.

top_50.name: BM-27 Uragan
top_50.notes: Russia ~200; Ukraine ~70. Used in several high-profile attacks.

top_50.name: BM-30 Smerch / Tornado-S
top_50.notes: Tornado-S fires guided rockets to 120 km. Ukraine also operated ~50 Smerch units.

top_50.name: 9K111 Fagot
top_50.notes: Soviet-era SACLOS ATGM from inherited stocks. 2,500m range.

top_50.name: 9K113 Konkurs
top_50.notes: Heavier successor to Fagot. 4,000m range. Remote-controlled launcher variant developed during war.

top_50.name: RK-3 Corsar
top_50.notes: Ukrainian lightweight shoulder-fired ATGM. Production surged after Feb 2022.

top_50.name: Panzerfaust 3
top_50.notes: 1,000+ supplied by Germany/Netherlands. Tandem warhead defeats ERA.

top_50.name: Carl Gustaf
top_50.notes: 100+ from Canada plus NATO allies. Credited with destroying first Russian T-90M.

top_50.name: SPG-9 Kopye
top_50.notes: Crew-served Soviet recoilless gun. Massive stockpiles on both sides.

top_50.name: AT4
top_50.notes: ~5,000 supplied by Sweden. Effective against lighter armor.

top_50.name: M72 LAW
top_50.notes: Supplied by USA, Canada, Norway, Denmark, Finland. Modern A7/A9/EC variants.

top_50.name: RPG-18 Mukha
top_50.notes: Millions produced. Also mounted on FPV drones by Ukrainian forces.

top_50.name: M142 HIMARS
top_50.notes: ~38 delivered. Disproportionate strategic impact despite small numbers. 9,500+ GMLRS expended.

top_50.name: PKP Pecheneg
top_50.notes: Improved PKM with forced air-cooled barrel. Used by Russian airborne and elite units.

key_patterns.soviet_dominance: Both sides rely heavily on Soviet-heritage platforms (AK-74M, PKM, SVD, D-30, 2S1, BM-21) due to massive Cold War stockpiles
key_patterns.ukraine_nato_transition: Ukraine is progressively transitioning to NATO-standard weapons (HK416, SCAR, M777, 155mm artillery) through Western aid
key_patterns.domestic_production: Ukraine's domestic industry (Stugna-P, Corsar, Bohdana, Malyuk, Fort-230) has been critical for sustainability
key_patterns.anti_tank_revolution: Javelin, NLAW, and Stugna-P fundamentally changed the armor-infantry balance in early 2022
key_patterns.artillery_war: Artillery accounts for ~80% of casualties; both sides burn through tubes and ammunition at industrial-scale rates
key_patterns.drone_adaptation: Shotguns and heavy MGs repurposed for anti-drone defense; RPG warheads mounted on FPV drones
key_patterns.manpads_diversity: Ukraine operates the most diverse MANPADS inventory of any conflict in recent history (7+ distinct systems)
